rag.description: Move the pointer inside an InvokeInputActions gesture, to an element, an offset, a viewport position, or a distance from where it is. The step checks its element and numbers before anything is sent, takes flexible parameters for target and duration, and keeps hovers and drags reliable.

qa.answer: It adds one pointer move to the input sequence of its InvokeInputActions container, without pressing or releasing a button.
qa.question: What does the AddPointerMove plugin do?

qa.answer: OnElement and Locator name an element to move to, X and Y set an offset or a position, Origin selects Pointer or Viewport, and Duration sets the time of the move. It stores no outputs.
qa.question: What are the key parameters and outputs of AddPointerMove?

qa.answer: It runs as an InputAction task step with the arrow-pointer icon and the ActionRuleModel, only as a child rule of InvokeInputActions, before the presses, releases, and scrolls it positions.
qa.question: How does AddPointerMove fit into an automation workflow?

qa.answer: Move to an element instead of a fixed position where possible, build a drag from several moves when a page needs more than one move event, and start a relative move from a known place.
qa.question: What are best practices for using AddPointerMove?

qa.answer: Use $type “Action” with pluginName “AddPointerMove”, with onElement for an element or with {{$ --X:200 --Y:150 --Origin:Viewport}} for a position, inside the rules of InvokeInputActions.
qa.question: How is an AddPointerMove rule configured?

qa.answer: A missing element, an unknown origin, or a value that is not a number fails the step, and the container then sends nothing. Outside InvokeInputActions the step fails with a message that names the container.

description: ### Purpose
AddPointerMove moves the pointer without pressing or releasing a button.
It runs only inside InvokeInputActions, where it sets the place of the presses, releases, and scrolls that follow it.
Flows use it to hover over a menu, to aim a click at an exact point, and to carry a pressed item to its drop target.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature | Description |
| Element target | Moves to the center of the element named by OnElement. |
| Offsets | Shifts the target by X and Y pixels from the element center. |
| Viewport position | Moves to an X and Y position measured from the top-left corner of the viewport. |
| Relative move | Moves by X and Y pixels from the current pointer position. |
| Timed move | Sets how long the driver spends on the move; whether it sends move events along the way depends on the driver, and ChromeDriver sends one at the end. |
| Loop element | Moves to the current element of a for-each loop when the rule names none. |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case | Description |
| Hover menus | Move over a menu so its items appear, then click an item the menu creates in a following container. |
| Drag and drop | Carry a pressed item from its source to its target. |
| Sliders | Drag a slider handle by an exact number of pixels. |
| Canvas work | Aim at a point of a canvas, a chart, or a map. |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case | Description |
| Hover states | Verify the tooltip or the style an element shows under the pointer. |
| Drag paths | Verify how a page reacts when an item is moved onto other elements, one AddPointerMove per element. |
| Position accuracy | Verify that a click at an exact offset hits the intended part of an element. |
### Platform
This plugin currently supports **Web** only.
Desktop and mobile drivers are not supported yet.

edge_cases: Element is covered by another element
annotations.expected_result: The pointer rests on the center of the menu button, which shows its hover state.
annotations.notes: The step runs only inside InvokeInputActions. An element that is not found fails the step, and the container sends nothing.

description: ### Move to the center of an element
The `onElement` value names the element with an XPath.
The pointer moves to its center over the default 250 milliseconds.

annotations.expected_result: The pointer rests 40 pixels right of and 10 pixels above the center of the slider track.
annotations.notes: Offsets are measured from the center of the element, not from its corner. An offset that leaves the viewport makes the driver reject the sequence.

description: ### Move to an offset from an element center
The element is found with a CSS selector, and X and Y shift the target from its center.
The move takes 400 milliseconds.

annotations.expected_result: The pointer rests 200 pixels from the left edge and 150 pixels from the top edge of the viewport.
annotations.notes: Viewport positions depend on the window size and the scroll position. Set the window size first when a flow relies on fixed positions.

description: ### Move to a position in the viewport
The Origin parameter measures X and Y from the top-left corner of the visible page.
The pointer moves to that point whatever element lies under it.

annotations.expected_result: The pointer ends 120 pixels right of where it was, after a move of one second.
annotations.notes: A relative move needs a known start, so move to an element first. The duration accepts a whole number of milliseconds or a time span.

description: ### Move by a distance from the current position
X and Y are measured from the current pointer position, which is the default origin.
With a button held by an earlier AddPointerDown, it drags a slider handle 120 pixels to the right.
Sets how long the move takes.
Accepts a whole number of milliseconds, such as `600`, or a time span, such as `00:00:01`.
Whether a longer duration adds move events depends on the driver; ChromeDriver sends one move at the end, so build a path from several AddPointerMove steps.
Defaults to 250 milliseconds, and a negative value or text that is not a duration fails the step.
parameters.name: Duration

description: Selects where X and Y are measured from when the rule names no element and inherits none from a for-each loop.
Defaults to Pointer, and any value other than Pointer or Viewport fails the step.
Ignored when the rule names or inherits an element.
parameters.name: Origin

description: Measures X and Y from the current pointer position.
Use it for a relative move, such as dragging a slider 120 pixels to the right.
values.name: Pointer

description: Measures X and Y from the top-left corner of the visible page.
Use it for an absolute position, such as a point on a full-page canvas.
values.name: Viewport

description: Sets the horizontal distance in pixels, where a positive value points right.
With a named or inherited element it is an offset from the element center; otherwise it is measured from Origin.
Defaults to 0, and text that is not a whole number fails the step.
parameters.name: X

description: Sets the vertical distance in pixels, where a positive value points down.
With a named or inherited element it is an offset from the element center; otherwise it is measured from Origin.
Defaults to 0, and text that is not a whole number fails the step.
parameters.name: Y

description: Holds the parameters of the move, such as `{{$ --X:200 --Y:150 --Origin:Viewport}}`.
A rule without an argument moves to the center of its element over 250 milliseconds.
A plain value such as `500` is ignored; set the time with `--Duration`.
properties.name: Argument

description: Selects how the OnElement value finds the element to move to.
Accepted values include Xpath, CssSelector, Id, LinkText, and PartialLinkText.
Defaults to Xpath, and is read only when OnElement is set.
properties.name: Locator

description: Names the element to move to, in the form the Locator selects.
The pointer goes to the center of the element, shifted by X and Y when they are set.
An element that is not found fails the step, and the container then sends nothing.
The element is found before the sequence is sent, so it must already be in the page; inside a for-each loop the search starts from the loop element.
properties.name: OnElement

summary: Adds a pointer move to the sequence of its InvokeInputActions container.
Moves to the center of an element, to an offset from that center, to a position in the viewport, or by a distance from the current pointer position.
Takes 250 milliseconds by default, and the Duration parameter sets how long the driver spends on the move.
